answer.rationale: The mandate and expiring contract create pressure to switch to the low-cost vendor, but memory_c2 only documents cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy—it says nothing about delivery reliability or quality under sustained full-volume load, which is the critical variable given the line is at 94% committed capacity with no buffer. Switching primary vendor now, without verified delivery performance data, risks the primary objective of not increasing delivery risk. Renewing incumbent alone doesn't meet the 18% cut mandate, and deferring isn't viable since the contract doesn't auto-renew in 14 days. Negotiating terms with the incumbent, using the low-cost quote as leverage (as memory_c4 shows worked before, and consistent with memory_c1/c6 showing incumbent stability and multi-year volume pricing), can recover meaningful margin without the unverified delivery risk of a full vendor switch. I verify memory_c2 first because it's the load-bearing claim for the riskier alternative action; if the archived record shows delivery performance was solid under volume, that would change the calculus toward switching or adding a second source instead.
